commonRules.statement: Use the selected brand and exact SKU/variant only. The official website is client-approved for its actual technical/CGI/certification/warranty statements; preserve issuer, scope, dates and qualifiers. Source approval is not output approval. All commercial offers come from the current brief. Reuse original technology artwork without reconstruction when depicting technical illustrations. When the selected owned-pdp v4 contract permits a sourced exterior-view alternative and omission of unresolved warranty/replacement claims, follow that slot-specific policy; do not require optional illustrations or claims to proceed. Do not introduce a standalone campaign master KV deliverable. Standing testing policy for both brands: source acceptance remains active until the user explicitly reinstates source-verification blocking. Do not block or fail solely for absent independent verification or repeat approval of the supplied website/brief statements. Do not expire this policy after a run or silently tighten it on retry. Generated artwork defects, invented claims and actual required source contradictions remain separate checks.

Before concepts, explain the selected format’s communication job, viewing context, one main proposition, supporting evidence, omitted content, native-versus-embedded copy, visual approach and action. Explain why the same brief changes treatment across destinations. Audience behaviour without evidence is a working hypothesis, not measured insight.

Treat playbooks as decision support, not fixed templates. Choose imagery, people, setting, lighting and graphic language from the brief and same-brand guidance. No default beige room, fixed photo box, mandatory people, blanket no-people rule or mandatory headline/body/CTA stack. Vary creative routes meaningfully while preserving facts and message.

Allocate copy roles and readable space together before rendering. If the content cannot fit, shorten optional copy, change composition or request an allowed extra module; never drop locked wording or qualifiers or shrink required text below useful reading size. OCR transcription alone cannot prove legibility.

Review the actual output in its intended container, crop, viewing size and sequence. Check message clarity, identity, source fidelity, required wording, legibility, action and delivery completeness. Distinguish observed defects from preferences; unknown is not pass. Only applicable client/platform contracts can block as requirements; recommendations guide critique and allow justified alternatives.

A treatment definition does not enable a renderer, publisher integration or native document format. Preserve missing-family/input limitations. Two options means two independently complete reviewed sets when requested; do not average away a failed child. Preserve versions, records and costs; no publishing or paid generation is authorized by this library.

The current user-authored brief is client-approved source authority for explicitly supplied offer/price/festive/EMI/bank terms and attributed expert proof or quotes, including their supplied approval/verification. Do not request separate independent verification or client reapproval solely for using those exact statements. Client-brief evidence records preserve complete supplied text and source provenance; they are not independent authentication. Preserve conditions, attribution, eligibility, dates and qualifiers. Do not invent missing values or imply a quote proves an unstated clinical outcome. Actual contradictions, absent required information, partner artwork availability and rendered errors remain separate checks. The exact-SKU official website is final client-approved source authority for technical/CGI, certifications, warranty and product statements; independent proof alone is not a prerequisite across formats.

For the editable-text workflow, strategy chooses the message and art direction reserves purposeful space on a real backdrop for the agreed hierarchy. Generate the scene without added campaign text; add agreed wording through editable layers afterward. Preserve genuine product markings and source technical artwork. Native titles/buttons stay in native fields. Review the final composite for copy fit, contrast, product occlusion and reading order. Image-only work may have no overlay; do not require a headline, CTA or emotional appeal merely to fill a layout.

packs.title: Instagram / Facebook feed

treatment.purpose: Make one proposition understandable during scrolling. Choose launch, benefit, occasion or proof from the brief; say why that proposition matters to the supplied audience.
treatment.copy: A concise headline may carry the idea; optional support must add evidence, not restate it. Keep a product identifier when recognition needs it. Put elaboration in the native caption, but never move an essential qualifier away from its claim.
treatment.visual: Choose product-led, human-use, editorial or contextual imagery for the message. Let one focal relationship dominate. Square needs compact hierarchy; portrait may give the product more context, not automatically more copy.
treatment.action: Choose one realistic next step. Organic posts can invite useful discussion or discovery; paid posts align the image promise with native CTA and landing page. A visual button is not an interactive control.
treatment.sequence: Each image is complete on its own. Two options explore different storytelling premises and meaningful composition choices while preserving the same proposition and facts.
treatment.inputs: Exact channel, organic/paid context, selected canvas, intended preview, brief audience/objective and scoped product references. Do not infer audience from the platform alone.
treatment.checks: Can the viewer identify what is being shown and the main point at normal feed width? Check required copy, qualifiers, product markings, crop and native-caption consistency.
treatment.avoid: Avoid feature dumps, arbitrary headline/body/CTA quotas, invented urgency, tiny legal text and stretching one landscape composition into portrait.

variants.square: Use a compact focal composition; do not shrink a wide multi-column design.
variants.portrait: Recompose for vertical inspection; protect product silhouette and preview crop.
variants.landscape: Short displayed height reduces copy capacity; put secondary explanation in native text.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Instagram / Facebook Story

treatment.purpose: Communicate one immediate takeaway in a full-screen, tap-through context. Decide whether the frame introduces, demonstrates, reminds or asks; a static frame cannot rely on motion to explain it.
treatment.copy: Prefer one short thought with only essential support. The viewer should understand it without stopping to decode a paragraph. Retain required qualifiers visibly; reduce the claim or request another frame if they cannot fit.
treatment.visual: Compose vertically from the start. Choose a purposeful product crop or complete view according to recognition needs; closer framing is a choice, not a rule. Reserve real scene space for the message and actual platform overlays.
treatment.action: Name the intended interaction: link sticker, native paid CTA, reply or no action. Reserve its area using the supplied preview/template. Do not paint a fake working sticker into the asset.
treatment.sequence: For a requested series, assign distinct context, evidence and action beats. Each frame should remain intelligible if adjacent frames are skipped. Do not generate extra frames without scope approval.
treatment.inputs: Organic versus paid, final interface preview, requested frame count, interaction destination and exact source assets. Use secondary safe-area guidance provisionally when official access is blocked.
treatment.checks: Inspect on a phone with header/footer/action overlays. Check time-to-understand qualitatively, copy legibility, crop, product identity and whether the action remains usable.
treatment.avoid: Avoid a feed poster centered in a tall empty canvas, dense text, automatic timers/urgency and universal safe-area percentages treated as verified policy.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Social carousel / connected slides

treatment.purpose: Choose a sequence because the story needs progression, comparison or explanation. State the reader’s question and why multiple slides help.
treatment.copy: The opening promises a specific useful takeaway; each subsequent slide adds a new fact, contrast or step. Use short signposts and retain local qualifiers on the slide carrying the claim.
treatment.visual: Create a consistent visual system with intentional rhythm: vary scale, framing or information structure as the story changes. Do not repeat the same product hero on every page without a distinct purpose.
treatment.action: Close with a useful synthesis and an appropriate next step. Do not put identical sales CTAs on every slide. Native captions and paid card destinations are separate fields.
treatment.sequence: Plan ordered page roles before rendering: hook/context → distinct explanation/evidence → synthesis/action as appropriate. Page count comes from the brief. Store one collection per concept with ordered children.
treatment.inputs: Requested count, platform/publishing mode, sequence purpose, evidence per claim, cover preview and any individual card destinations.
treatment.checks: Review slides individually and as a set: missing/duplicate pages, progression, contradiction, continuity, numbering and cover-to-final promise fulfilment. Partial sets cannot pass whole-set review.
treatment.avoid: Avoid resize-only slides, filler to reach the count, unsupported before/after claims, orphan qualifiers and confusing carousel ads with native document posts.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: LinkedIn feed image

treatment.purpose: Choose the relevant professional or corporate angle from the brief: product launch, company news, partner update, useful insight or employer story. LinkedIn does not automatically turn a consumer mattress into a B2B proposition.
treatment.copy: Use an informative headline and a small amount of evidence where needed. Keep introductory/native text separate. Prefer a precise insight over a slogan or corporate jargon; preserve names, roles and source wording.
treatment.visual: Use a credible focal product, person, chart or scene that makes the point visible. Keep typography comfortable in the selected landscape/square/portrait preview; tall imagery does not imply desktop eligibility.
treatment.action: One action consistent with the objective and native destination. Awareness need not force a purchase button; an announcement can invite reading the actual source.
treatment.sequence: Single images stand alone; requested variants preserve the same facts but recompose. Long explanations should be separately scoped as documents/carousels rather than squeezed into the graphic.
treatment.inputs: Audience supplied by brief, corporate facts, actual channel/device context, reference imagery and selected placement contract.
treatment.checks: Check headline comprehension, proof accuracy, readable support/CTA, actual product markings, native-copy consistency and preview on each intended device.
treatment.avoid: Avoid dense presentation slides, tiny footer proof, generic boardroom imagery unrelated to the brief, and treating platform character limits as embedded-image copy targets.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: LinkedIn document / slide publication

treatment.purpose: Develop a useful argument or learning resource that rewards advancing through pages. Specify what the reader will understand or decide by the end.
treatment.copy: Make the cover promise concrete. Give each page one argument with evidence; prefer plain headings, short explanations and labelled charts. Keep citations close to their claims.
treatment.visual: Use a readable page grid and consistent section markers. Design for page viewing on a phone as well as the downloadable document; avoid dense slide-deck screenshots.
treatment.action: Close with a relevant next step and source/contact information when supplied. Gated access and lead forms belong to native publishing setup.
treatment.sequence: Outline cover, context, evidence/application and conclusion; verify reading order, completeness, references and page numbers across the document.
treatment.inputs: Authored source content, audience, approved facts, requested page count, native document profile and digital accessibility needs.
treatment.checks: Inspect all pages at intended preview width, selectable text/accessibility when supported, hyperlinks and exported page order. Raster slides alone do not establish an accessible PDF.
treatment.avoid: Avoid inventing research, using fonts below readable size to hit a page quota, and calling a set of PNGs a fully editable document.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: YouTube Community image

treatment.purpose: Start a useful conversation, reveal a relevant update or preview related content for the existing audience. This is a post, not automatically a video thumbnail.
treatment.copy: Let the native post text provide context. Use minimal embedded wording only when necessary for the image to make sense; do not invent a video title, claim or release date.
treatment.visual: Keep the key subject and message clear in the feed’s square preview; inspect expanded view for any portrait or landscape asset. Choose imagery tied to the post’s actual subject.
treatment.action: Use a real question, related content destination or no CTA. Do not imply a playable image, poll or working button when the publishing format does not provide it.
treatment.sequence: Multiple images, if requested, should add distinct views or explanations with a clear order and consistent identity.
treatment.inputs: Post intent, related content if any, selected image count and native post copy. Delivery support must be explicit; do not substitute a thumbnail route.
treatment.checks: Check square preview, full expanded image, relationship with native text, authenticity and requested set completeness.
treatment.avoid: Avoid clickbait that the post cannot fulfil, tiny thumbnail-like captions and treating a Community post as a 16:9 video cover.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: YouTube thumbnail

treatment.purpose: Represent the actual linked video with an immediately recognisable visual promise. Curiosity must be resolved by the video, not invented drama.
treatment.copy: Use optional concise text that complements the video title. Avoid copying the whole title into the picture or adding unsupported comparisons.
treatment.visual: Use a strong subject relationship and intelligible silhouette at thumbnail size. Keep key details away from actual interface overlays such as duration. Preserve faces/product identity.
treatment.action: The real action is opening the video. Do not simulate extra playback controls or claim results absent from the video.
treatment.sequence: Each thumbnail is a complete alternative for the same video; keep experiments distinct without altering the factual promise.
treatment.inputs: Actual video topic/title, authentic stills or permitted product imagery, target platform profile and overlay preview.
treatment.checks: Review tiny feed preview and full export; verify content promise, identity, crop, file specification and non-misleading treatment.
treatment.avoid: Avoid applying Community-post assumptions or inventing testimony, reactions and results.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Pinterest image / Pin

treatment.purpose: Offer an idea worth saving or exploring: a use, setting, product solution or practical guide. The Pin should remain understandable outside the original posting moment.
treatment.copy: Add an informative text cue only when it clarifies the idea. Keep detailed discovery terms and description in native fields; avoid unreadable keyword stuffing in artwork.
treatment.visual: Make the subject/product easy to recognise in a vertical browsing grid. Let useful setting details support the idea while preserving hierarchy and actual product appearance.
treatment.action: Match the destination to the depicted idea/product. Native product tags and links are separate; do not draw fake shopping controls.
treatment.sequence: Each Pin is self-contained; collections may explore different practical ideas, not duplicate a single crop.
treatment.inputs: Destination, idea/topic, product source and selected organic/paid profile. Do not extrapolate one Pin type’s rules to all others.
treatment.checks: Check grid-preview readability, subject visibility, brand/product recognition and promise-to-destination agreement.
treatment.avoid: Avoid noisy collages without a clear organising idea, unnecessary overlay text and false claims of guaranteed saves or clicks.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: PMax / responsive display asset set

treatment.purpose: Define one coherent product/audience theme per asset group. Provide complementary visual routes that can work with separately assembled headlines, logos and actions.
treatment.copy: Prefer imagery that can combine with native text without duplication. Apply the selected profile’s overlay policy; any permitted embedded words must remain meaningful in multiple combinations.
treatment.visual: Create distinct landscape, square and portrait compositions. Preserve focal subjects through expected crop and assembly; clean product/context imagery should carry the meaning.
treatment.action: Native CTA and destination govern action. Keep business name and logo assets separate where the campaign uses native brand controls; do not treat a flattened poster as the full asset group.
treatment.sequence: Deliver the requested ratio/slot inventory with consistent SKU and proposition. Quantity recommendations never authorize extra generation. Check combinations, not only isolated files.
treatment.inputs: Campaign type, asset-group theme, required slots, native copy/logo assets and landing page. Required publisher fields remain separate from image production.
treatment.checks: Check all required assets, native combinations, crops, consistency and each file’s constraints. A raster export does not prove account acceptance or campaign performance.
treatment.avoid: Avoid one resized poster everywhere, collages that become illegible when assembled, baked fake controls and mixing unrelated products into an asset group.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Fixed-size display banner

treatment.purpose: Communicate a single relevant proposition in a small, externally placed rectangle. Decide the minimum useful product cue, brand cue and action for each exact size.
treatment.copy: Use compact copy appropriate to the actual pixel height. At very short sizes, simplify the proposition rather than miniaturise the whole campaign. Essential qualifiers must still be readable or the claim must change.
treatment.visual: Re-layout wide, square and tall banners separately. Let product, headline and action have clear relative priorities; do not make tiny photoreal details responsible for recognition.
treatment.action: Use one truthful action that the actual destination fulfils. Follow the selected profile on graphical controls; never simulate unavailable close/download/play functions.
treatment.sequence: A banner set has one inventory row per requested size, all tied to one message and supplied offer; no silent omission of difficult small sizes.
treatment.inputs: Exact placement dimensions/file cap, campaign objective, destination, claim/offer terms and inventory list.
treatment.checks: Inspect at 100% actual exported size, file weight, clipping, qualifier readability and completeness across sizes.
treatment.avoid: Avoid scaling down a social poster, unreadable legal lines and a universal font-size claim across physically different previews.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Website desktop / mobile hero

treatment.purpose: Orient the visitor and make the page promise clear. Decide whether the image demonstrates the product, establishes context or supports a live HTML proposition.
treatment.copy: Prefer live HTML for the headline, supporting text and button when the component supports it. Do not generate duplicate text inside the image; baked-copy requests require their own crop and readability checks.
treatment.visual: Plan desktop and mobile compositions around real component bounds and focal point. Use a separate mobile image when the desktop scene cannot survive cropping. Natural negative space must be intentional, not added haze.
treatment.action: The site’s real button and destination carry the action. Reserve space for actual text overlays and avoid confusing image-based buttons with working controls.
treatment.sequence: Treat desktop/mobile sources, focal coordinates, alt text and component usage as one responsive handoff. Preserve the same product and page promise across variants.
treatment.inputs: Actual component widths/heights, breakpoint/crop behaviour, live text/CTA placement, loading/performance budget and product source.
treatment.checks: Render in the real component at laptop and mobile widths, with text wrapping and crop. Inspect focal preservation, overlap, alt purpose and actual bytes; standalone-image review is insufficient.
treatment.avoid: Avoid assuming one universal hero size, forcing desktop text into a mobile crop, depicting CTA as a decorative object or claiming source resolution from upscaled export dimensions.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Website / app promotional banner

treatment.purpose: Support a specific page task or campaign message without competing with page navigation and primary content.
treatment.copy: Use one concise proposition. Keep supplied price, dates and material terms together. Prefer native page text where available; secondary terms cannot disappear on mobile.
treatment.visual: Design for the banner’s actual displayed short height, real container crop and adjacent UI. Prioritise one recognisable product or visual motif.
treatment.action: Use the component’s real click target and destination; state whether the whole banner or a native button is clickable.
treatment.sequence: Desktop/mobile variants form one delivery set. If a narrow version cannot preserve the message and qualifier, change the layout or request an alternate component.
treatment.inputs: Component template, breakpoint sizes, baked-versus-live copy decision, destination and current brief offer terms.
treatment.checks: Check smallest rendered instance, hover/focus styling owned by the site, crop and message consistency. Verify destination mapping separately from image appearance.
treatment.avoid: Avoid giant campaign headlines in shallow strips, unreadable footnotes, redundant buttons and using outdated website prices as brief input.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Category tiles / landing-page modules

treatment.purpose: Give each module a role in the page journey: navigate, demonstrate, explain, compare or reassure. Prioritise the user’s next decision, not a random collection of visuals.
treatment.copy: Tile labels should distinguish destinations. Explanation modules use concise headings and real evidence; long details belong in selectable page content.
treatment.visual: Keep visual scale and crop consistent across sibling tiles. Give each module a distinct visual job; art-direct with neighbouring modules and mobile stacking in mind.
treatment.action: Map every tile/module to the intended native destination or action. Do not repeat a purchase CTA on every informational block.
treatment.sequence: Outline the complete page sequence before creating assets. Review whether the sequence answers the brief’s main uncertainty and avoids repeating the hero.
treatment.inputs: Page wireframe, module IDs/order, product/category scope, responsive template and destinations.
treatment.checks: Inspect within page context: sequence, mobile stacking, image/text pairing, crop, alt text and missing modules.
treatment.avoid: Avoid calling a folder of banners a landing page, using inconsistent product scale or filling unsupported modules with invented proof.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Article / blog / Open Graph image

treatment.purpose: Represent the specific article or announcement honestly and make it recognisable when shared outside the site.
treatment.copy: Use optional short title/context. The page title and social-preview text are separate; do not bake the entire article summary into the image.
treatment.visual: Choose an image that explains the article’s subject. Protect the essential focal area across site and share previews; distinguish conceptual illustration from factual photography.
treatment.action: The share card links to the article. Avoid unrelated sales buttons or implying proof not present in the article.
treatment.sequence: Provide each requested site/share variant separately with consistent subject and title; a feed landscape image is not automatically a validated OG image.
treatment.inputs: Actual article title/content, destination, CMS/share requirements and allowed imagery.
treatment.checks: Check source-content accuracy, preview crop, useful alt text and title/image agreement; test actual metadata rendering separately.
treatment.avoid: Avoid fabricated studies, editorial imagery presented as real events and using nearby dimensions as an exact requested export.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Marketplace MAIN / listing hero

treatment.purpose: Make the item being sold unmistakable. This slot serves product identification and inspection, not a campaign story.
treatment.copy: Respect the selected marketplace/category policy for added text, logos and graphics. Physical product labels are different from promotional overlays.
treatment.visual: Show the exact purchasable variant with accurate colour, proportions, finish and included parts. Use the required background/framing for the actual marketplace template; never borrow another store’s rules.
treatment.action: Purchase actions belong to the listing interface. No painted CTA, invented badge or contextual accessory that implies an included item.
treatment.sequence: Keep MAIN separate from secondary gallery and A+ modules. Provide the exact requested variants rather than treating one generic hero as every SKU.
treatment.inputs: Marketplace/store/category, applicable MAIN template, exact SKU/variant, included-item facts and source photographs.
treatment.checks: Check product identity, inclusion accuracy, background/framing, graphics policy, actual resolution and category-specific requirements. Mark account/category rules unknown when absent.
treatment.avoid: Avoid lifestyle scenes where disallowed, multiple variants shown as one purchase, invented certification stamps and claiming platform certification from an image review.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Supplemental listings / product gallery

treatment.purpose: Answer inspection and purchase questions through complementary views and evidence. Select roles from the category and brief rather than copying a fixed mattress story into every product.
treatment.copy: Photography can stand without copy. Information tiles use short sourced statements and nearby qualifiers. Exact dimensions and ownership terms remain source-bound.
treatment.visual: Use full views, material detail, supported dimensions, context and included-item explanation as relevant. Technical construction/CGI must reuse the exact website asset unchanged.
treatment.action: Listing UI carries the buying action. Avoid repeated sales buttons in product information unless the actual destination explicitly permits and calls for them.
treatment.sequence: Define ordered slots and one purpose per slot. Complete the requested inventory; a repeated hero does not fill a missing source-dependent role. Full owned PDP uses its existing twelve-slot contract.
treatment.inputs: Destination, requested slot plan, exact SKU sources, official technical images, dimensions and ownership facts.
treatment.checks: Inspect individual readability/identity and whole-set coverage, contradictions, duplicates and missing slots. Keep included-product/context props distinguishable.
treatment.avoid: Avoid interpreting source photographs as warranty proof, inventing internal geometry or calling a partial set complete.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Marketplace A+ / enhanced modules

treatment.purpose: Reduce purchase uncertainty through a coherent module narrative. Choose benefits, evidence, usage or comparisons based on what the listing still needs to explain.
treatment.copy: Use the native text fields available in the chosen module. Keep embedded text sparse and readable; retain nearby qualifiers. Product marketing rules can restrict otherwise brief-approved offers or claims.
treatment.visual: Design to each actual module slot, not one stretched strip. Use source-preserved technology artwork and supporting product/context imagery with a consistent visual system.
treatment.action: Use only actions/links actually supported by the marketplace module. No off-platform sales button or simulated interaction in a static image.
treatment.sequence: Plan module purpose and order before images. Remove repetition across hero, benefit, technology and comparison blocks. Keep one collection with complete module children per concept.
treatment.inputs: Marketplace/account, Basic versus other tier, approved template slots, native field definitions, eligibility and exact product evidence.
treatment.checks: Inspect the composed module set in desktop/mobile publisher previews, embedded and native text, comparison scope, claims and asset inventory. A successful image is not a submitted A+ page.
treatment.avoid: Avoid microscopic text, image-only long paragraphs, confusing A+ with MAIN listing rules, and assuming US template/policy details certify an Indian account.

packs.authority: Studio recommendations informed by sources; exact selected placement contracts and client requirements take precedence.

packs.title: Premium A+ static assets

treatment.purpose: Use Premium only where the account/template is confirmed and the brief needs richer explanation. Larger imagery should improve product understanding, not increase text density.
treatment.copy: Allocate copy to real native modules such as questions, comparisons or hotspot descriptions. Never bake interactive content into a flat image and claim it works.
treatment.visual: Art-direct each selected high-resolution module and its mobile crop. Keep focal product detail inspectable and source-preserved technology elements intact.
treatment.action: Native carousel, hotspot, question and comparison behaviour belongs to publisher configuration. Deliver the static assets and content mapping with unsupported interactions explicit.
treatment.sequence: Map modules, states and child assets in an ordered manifest. Variants are complete sets; do not substitute Basic A+ when Premium is requested.
treatment.inputs: Confirmed Premium eligibility, exact module schema, required static states, native text, selected SKU sources and mobile templates.
treatment.checks: Check every required static asset against the real module, logical order, state mapping and publisher preview. Missing interaction implementation cannot be labelled complete.
treatment.avoid: Avoid assuming eligibility, auto-adding video, marketing performance guarantees or treating one wide image as a Premium experience.
